questions.a: Distance is the total path length (scalar); displacement is the shortest straight distance from start to end with direction (vector).

questions.q: Can displacement be zero while distance is not? Give an example.
questions.a: Yes - going around a circular track once: distance is the circumference, displacement is zero.

questions.q: What does a position-time graph tell us?
questions.a: Its slope gives the speed; a straight sloping line means uniform motion.

questions.q: What does a distance-time graph with a straight line show?
questions.a: Uniform speed - equal distances in equal times.

questions.q: What does a curved distance-time graph indicate?
questions.a: Changing (non-uniform) speed - the body speeds up if the curve steepens.

questions.q: What does the slope of a velocity-time graph give?
questions.a: Acceleration; the area under the graph gives distance travelled.
